title: Empty-queue solution for live deployment first impression
description: Reviewer hits colacop.foramerica.dev → currently sees nothing. Two candidate solutions (sprint-order.md flags both): (a) pre-load fixtures into the deployed instance so results are visible on first load, by running the watcher on fixtures/ at deploy time; (b) helpful empty-state UI with example fixtures linked for download and a 'drop pairs into the watched directory to try' invitation. Both are defensible; pick one or both based on what's faster after T8 lands.
design:
OPTION A — Pre-load fixtures into the deployed instance:
- At deploy time, after migrations run, copy fixtures/labels/* and fixtures/applications/* into data/incoming/ on the box and let the watcher process them once. Results live in the DB; the queue is non-empty on first load.
- Pro: zero UI change; the agent sees the same UI they would see with real submissions.
- Con: the fixture jobs persist in the queue forever unless decided. Could decide them all 'approve' programmatically as part of seeding so they sit in the 'Decided' filter rather than the active queue, but then reviewer sees an empty active queue again unless they specifically click 'Decided'.

OPTION B — Helpful empty-state UI:
- When listJobs returns zero rows in the active queue, render an empty-state panel: 'No submissions in the queue. To try the prototype, drop a label image and matching application JSON into data/incoming/ on this server, or use the upload form below. Sample fixtures: <links to fixtures/labels/cointreau.jpg etc>.'
- Pro: teaches the reviewer what to do; doesn't pollute the active queue.
- Con: requires reviewer action to see anything.

OPTION C — Both:
- Pre-load fixtures into the queue (Option A) leaving them undecided so they show in the active queue. Reviewer sees real findings on first load, plus the upload form for trying their own. The empty-state panel is unnecessary because the queue is non-empty.
- Pro: best demo experience.
- Con: the prototype's 'active queue' visibly contains fixture jobs that aren't real work; document this clearly in the empty-state-shaped 'sample submissions' callout above the queue table.

RECOMMEND OPTION C unless time forces A or B alone. Implementation: a one-shot npm run seed:fixtures script that copies from fixtures/ to data/incoming/ and waits for processing; called from the deploy procedure (cc-ckg) on the live box only; not run in local dev unless explicitly invoked.

DEPS: cc-7w9 (so the seed produces real Gemini findings, not stub defaults), cc-ckg (so there is a deployed instance to seed).
acceptance_criteria:
1. The chosen option is documented in a short notes/empty-queue-decision.md so the rationale is preserved.
2. On a fresh deploy, https://colacop.foramerica.dev shows non-empty content (queue with fixtures, or empty-state panel, or both) on the very first page load.
3. The implementation does not require manual SSH steps after the deploy command sequence — whatever solution is chosen runs automatically as part of cc-ckg's deploy script or the seed npm script.
4. typecheck/lint/test pass.

description: UC-001 step 4 explicitly asks the system to show, per comparable field, the value extracted from the label and the value supplied in the application, side by side. Restructure the Layer 2 section as columns: field name | extracted value | application value | verdict | message. Same restructure or a simpler version may suit Layer 1 if useful.
design:
src/web/App.tsx JobDetailView:
- Layer 2 section restructures from row-per-field-with-message to a table: columns 'Field | Extracted | Application | Verdict | Reason'.
- Each row's 'Extracted' shows the extracted ExtractedField value (need API response to include it; today the API returns Layer 2 results without the underlying extracted values, so the API needs to include extracted_fields alongside).

API:

- GET /api/jobs/:id should include the parsed ApplicationData (currently includes application_path; the UI would have to fetch and parse, which is fine, but cleaner to include the parsed JSON in the response).

title: Wire real Gemini provider; replace stub in worker startup
description: Stub LabelProvider is the proximate blocker on testing the prototype with real labels — it returns identical canned data for any unknown stem so all three real bottles in fixtures/labels/ currently produce identical findings (good-merlot defaults). Wire a GeminiLabelProvider implementing LabelProvider.analyzeLabel(imagePath) by calling Gemini's vision API with structured-JSON output matching the existing ExtractedFields shape, and select the provider in worker startup based on env var presence (GEMINI_API_KEY). While here, extend ExtractedFields with countryOfOrigin so Layer 2 can actually compare it.
design:
FILES:
- NEW: src/core/providers/gemini.ts implementing LabelProvider.
- EDIT: src/core/schemas.ts — add countryOfOrigin to ExtractedFields (also as ExtractedField with confidence) + applicationDataSchema already has it.
- EDIT: src/core/verification.ts — runLayer2 compareCountryOfOrigin should now use the extracted value instead of the placeholder needs_review note.
- EDIT: src/core/providers/stub.ts — add countryOfOrigin to fixtures (undefined or blank for domestic; could add an import fixture later).
- EDIT: src/worker/index.ts — import both providers; choose based on process.env['GEMINI_API_KEY'] presence; log which is in use at startup.
- NEW or EDIT: .env.example with GEMINI_API_KEY=.
- EDIT: README.md — one-line note that real extraction requires GEMINI_API_KEY; without it, the worker falls back to the stub.

SDK: @google/genai is the current package name as of 2026 (verify against current docs — knowledge cutoff may be stale; older docs reference @google/generative-ai). Model id: latest Gemini 3.x Pro vision tier (verify; expect gemini-3-pro or similar). Auth via API key in env.

IMAGE INPUT: read file as bytes from imagePath; pass via inline_data (base64) for files <20MB. Composites in fixtures/labels/ are <600KB so inline is fine. No need to use the Files API.

STRUCTURED OUTPUT: use responseMimeType: 'application/json' + responseSchema. Schema fields:
  brandName, classType, alcoholContent, netContents, producerName, producerAddress, countryOfOrigin (optional), governmentWarning.
Each: { value: string | null, confidence: 'low'|'med'|'hi', confidenceRaw: number | null }.

PROMPT (place in a const at top of gemini.ts):
'This image shows the front and/or back panels of an alcohol bottle label, possibly as a side-by-side or stacked composite of two panels. Extract each listed field as it appears on the label. Return null for any field not visible in the image. Do not hallucinate or infer missing values from training data — if the back panel is not visible, the government warning field must be null. For each field, return extraction_confidence: low (blurry, partial, glare-obscured, hard to read), med (readable but stylized or low-contrast), or hi (clean print, unambiguous).'

NULL HANDLING: when Gemini returns null for a field's value, transform to { value: '', confidence: 'low', confidenceRaw: null }. runLayer1's checkRequiredField already treats empty value as fail (mandatory field missing). countryOfOrigin null → leave as undefined (it's optional).

CONFIDENCE_RAW: if the SDK returns logprobs or a numeric self-rating, map to 0-1. If only the bucketed string is returned, derive confidenceRaw as 0.3 (low) / 0.7 (med) / 0.95 (hi) for now — better than null for downstream tuning, and the bucketed value is what the UI uses anyway.

OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS BEAD: prompt iteration / model choice tuning beyond making it work; per-field side-by-side detail UI (separate P1 bead); production deploy (separate bead T8).
acceptance_criteria:
1. npm install succeeds with the chosen Gemini SDK package added.
2. src/core/providers/gemini.ts exists implementing LabelProvider.analyzeLabel(imagePath).
3. With GEMINI_API_KEY set in env, dropping fixtures/labels/cointreau.jpg + fixtures/applications/cointreau.json into data/incoming/ produces Layer 1 + Layer 2 findings whose values reflect what is actually printed on the cointreau bottle (not the good-merlot defaults).
4. Same test passes for agave and rumble fixtures.
5. Without GEMINI_API_KEY set, src/worker/index.ts falls back to StubLabelProvider and logs which provider is in use at startup.
6. ExtractedFields includes countryOfOrigin; Layer 2 compares it normally when present in both extraction and application; reports needs_application_data when missing from application.
7. Empty/null values from Gemini map to { value: '', confidence: 'low', confidenceRaw: null }, and Layer 1's checkRequiredField marks them as fail with the standard mandatory-field-missing message.
8. .env.example contains GEMINI_API_KEY= (no value).
9. README.md briefly notes the env var requirement and the stub fallback.
10. npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run test all pass.
close_reason: Wired GeminiLabelProvider with @google/genai (gemini-3.1-pro-preview); structured-JSON output, null→empty for required fields; countryOfOrigin added as optional ExtractedField with full Layer 2 comparison; worker selects provider by GEMINI_API_KEY presence; 3 fixture application JSONs added; verified end-to-end against 3 real bottle photos.

title: Layer 1 ABV regex too narrow; rejects formats Gemini commonly returns
description:
Observed during cc-7w9 live testing: alcoholContent Layer 1 fails for cointreau (40%), agave (no ABV on photo, expected fail), and rumble (47%) — Cointreau and Rumble both have clearly readable ABVs on the label.

The two regexes in src/core/verification.ts (ABV_FORMAT and ABV_SHORTHAND) require the literal token 'alcohol' or 'alc' to appear adjacent to the percentage. Gemini-returned strings like '40% Alc/Vol', 'ALC. 47% BY VOL.', or '40% ABV' likely fall outside these patterns.

Need to broaden parseAbv to accept:
- 'X% ABV' (no 'vol' / 'volume' suffix)
- 'ALC. X% BY VOL.' (period on 'alc.', period on 'vol.')
- 'X% Alc/Vol' (no leading 'alc')
- 'X%ALC/VOL' (no spaces)

Until this is fixed, every real Gemini extraction reports Layer 1 alcohol-format failure regardless of what's actually on the label, which masks both real failures and successes.

Suggested approach: build a small fixture of Gemini-observed ABV string variants from the live test runs, then iterate the regex against it. Consider extracting parseAbv into its own module so we can keep the test file focused.

title: Worker should refuse to start if another worker is already bound to the same DATABASE_URL/INCOMING_DIR
description:
Observed during cc-7w9 live testing: stale 'tsx watch src/worker/index.ts' processes from earlier dev sessions silently raced with my fresh worker. Both watched the same data/incoming and both inserted into the same Postgres. On a single fixture drop, chokidar fired add events to all running workers; the stub-backed stale worker won the race for Layer 1 (16ms — clearly stub) and the new Gemini-backed worker overwrote Layer 2 with a real extraction. The combined record looked corrupt (Layer 1 said '13.5% ABV pass' against the actual Cointreau label) and was confusing to debug.

There's no single-writer guarantee in the worker right now. ps aux is the only way to notice.

Suggested approach: take an advisory lock on a stable key (e.g., pg_advisory_lock(hashtext(INCOMING_DIR))) at worker startup. If the lock can't be acquired, log and exit non-zero rather than running silently. Optionally: also lock per-job-stem during processStem to harden against accidental double-starts in future deploy mishaps.

Out of scope: orchestrating multiple workers across machines (PM2 fork mode, etc.) — that needs a separate design pass.

title: Pick SQL access library: Knex vs Kysely
description: ARCHITECTURE.md currently picks Knex; Chair is leaning toward Kysely. Tower writes a short comparison covering: type-safety with TS-strict (Kysely's strength), migration ergonomics (Knex's strength, mature CLI), reviewer familiarity (Knex more conventional, Kysely growing), ecosystem maturity, exit cost if we change later. Output: a 1-paragraph decision recorded in ARCHITECTURE.md and a rewrite of the existing Knex mentions in 'Chosen Stack', 'Why This Stack', and 'Database Responsibilities' sections. Blocks cc-scz so scaffolding doesn't bake in the wrong choice.
notes: Decision: Kysely. Rationale: schema-first type inference aligns with the project's strict TS rules (no any, no casts, noUncheckedIndexedAccess); the shared Database interface doubles as documentation between API and worker; column typos become compile errors. Migration tooling gap (no Knex-style CLI) is small at our scale — a tsx-driven Migrator script is sufficient for ~4-6 expected migrations. Reviewer surprise minimal in 2026. ARCHITECTURE.md updated; cc-scz design notes updated to install kysely + pg + tsx.

title: Author Cockburn-style use cases
description: Critical path: write UC-001 (Verify an alcohol label application) in design/use-cases.yaml so architecture and the prototype scope can be checked against an actor-and-goal-level description. cc-xog has shipped a working stub of the system without a use case ever being written; re-grounding the design via UC-001 is the first action in the May 1 replan. Cockburn-style: ONE main use case with rich extensions, NOT a scattershot of UC-001/UC-002/UC-003. Source material is the existing facts and requirements; do NOT look at src/ or the running app while drafting (that anchors the use case on the implementation rather than on the agent's goal).

FRESH TOWER: read CLAUDE.md, prompts/tower.md, CONTEXT.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, then discovery/sources/S-001..S-005, discovery/facts.yaml, design/requirements.yaml, docs/handoff.md. Do NOT open src/, the running UI, or browse the deployed URL — those anchor the use case on the implementation instead of the agent's goal.

OUTPUT: create design/use-cases.yaml (file does not yet exist). Schema:

use_cases:
  - id: UC-001
    title: 'Verify an alcohol label application'
    primary_actor: 'TTB compliance agent'
    scope: 'colacop prototype'
    level: 'user goal'    # Cockburn level
    preconditions:
      - '...'
    success_guarantee:
      - '...'
    main_success_scenario:
      - step: 1
        actor_action: '...'
        system_response: '...'
    extensions:
      - id: 'UC-001.3a'   # extends step 3 of main scenario
        condition: '...'
        steps:
          - '...'
    supports_requirements:
      - REQ-001
    references_facts:
      - F-004
    out_of_scope:
      - '...'
    open_questions:
      - '...'

EXTENSIONS TO COVER (per docs/handoff.md, expand or merge as needed): submitted file already processed; submitted file still queued or processing; batch of files arrives; extracted field clearly matches application data; extracted field clearly mismatches application data; brand differs only by case/punctuation and needs tolerant matching; government warning text/capitalization fails strict matching; label image is unreadable or low confidence; model provider is unavailable or blocked; application data arrives without label; label arrives without application data.

LEVEL DISCIPLINE: stay at user-goal level. Refer to 'the system' not 'the watcher', 'the queue' not 'data/incoming/', 'the verification result' not 'Layer 1 / Layer 2 / lifecycle / verdict'. Architecture-shaped detail (lifecycle states, verdict enums, watcher mechanics, Kysely schema) belongs in ARCHITECTURE.md and stays there. The use case is an agent's narrative, not a sequence diagram.

CITATIONS: every extension must cite at least one supporting fact (F-XXX) and at least one supported requirement (REQ-XXX). If you find an extension that lacks fact backing, flag it in open_questions — do not invent fact provenance.

FOLLOW-UP: a separate bead covers the WILL/WON'T/MAYBE scope pass and the structured audit. Do not try to do those here — UC-001 first, full-scope (canonical product), then the next session decides what's in for May 1 submission.

UC-001 is present with all Cockburn fields (id, title, primary_actor, scope, level, preconditions, success_guarantee, main_success_scenario, extensions, supports_requirements, references_facts, out_of_scope, open_questions). 3. Main success scenario is 6-12 numbered steps with actor_action + system_response per step. 4. Extensions cover the 11 listed cases (or merge them with explicit rationale). 5. Each extension cites at least one F-XXX fact and one REQ-XXX requirement. 6. No reference to lifecycle enum values, verdict enum values, watcher specifics, Kysely, React, Express, or any other implementation detail. 7. Ruby validation passes: ruby -e 'require "yaml"; YAML.load_file("design/use-cases.yaml"); puts "YAML OK"'. 8. title: Build sample-label fixtures and application-data fixtures
description: Build a realistic fixture set covering the main verification paths. Source mix: real bottles from Chair's cabinet (preferred for realism per assignment F-039/F-040/F-041 — Jenny Park's interview specifically calls out 'labels photographed at weird angles, lighting is bad, glare on the bottle') and/or AI-generated labels (preferred for absolute-baseline-correct happy path). Each fixture is one image (.jpg/.png/.webp) paired with one application-data JSON sharing a filename stem. Necks are out of scope for this prototype — document in README; in the real TTB COLA system labels include front/back/neck panels but we treat one composite image as one submission. Real bottles are typically photographed as a front+back composite (stitched in Preview) so the government warning panel is included; some fixtures may intentionally omit the back panel to exercise the missing-warning path.
design:
FIXTURE COMPOSITION (target ~6-8 fixtures):
- 2-3 clean front+back composites (real bottles or AI-generated) with well-formed application JSON that matches the label exactly. Exercises the happy-path 'all WILL paths succeed' demo.
- 1 fixture where brand name on the label differs from the application by case/punctuation only (e.g. 'STONE'S THROW' on label, 'Stone's Throw' in JSON) per F-030. Exercises Layer 2 brand drift / fuzzy match.
- 1 fixture where the application's alcohol_content disagrees with the label's printed value beyond the F-052 wine tolerance. Exercises Layer 2 mismatch with rule-based explanation.
- 1 fixture intentionally missing the back panel (front-only photo). Exercises Layer 1 missing-government-warning path; demonstrates honest reporting rather than hallucination.
- 1 fixture photographed badly on purpose (glare, angle, low contrast, or stylized/foil label). Exercises REQ-009 / F-056 low extraction_confidence path; the system should flag low confidence rather than guess.
- 1 fixture where the label's government warning has a real violation (lowercase 'Government Warning' instead of all-caps, or near-text-but-not-exact wording, per F-047/F-048 and Jenny's interview). Exercises Layer 1 warning strict-match failure.

STORAGE: fixtures/ at repo root. Subdirs: fixtures/labels/ (the .jpg/.png pairs), fixtures/applications/ (the .json pairs sharing stems), fixtures/README.md (one paragraph per fixture: stem, source, what it tests, expected verdict pattern).

NO PII / COPYRIGHT CONCERNS: real bottles are Chair's own; this is take-home demo use, not commercial distribution. Brand names are real; that is fine.

GEMINI PROMPTING (informs cc-htd boundary, executed in the Gemini-wiring bead later): the prompt to analyzeLabel should explicitly state 'this image shows the front and/or back panels of an alcohol bottle label, possibly as a side-by-side or stacked composite. Extract the listed fields. Return null for any field not visible. Do not hallucinate missing fields.' Use Gemini's native structured-output / JSON-schema mode rather than freeform-text-plus-parse. Per-field extraction_confidence (low/med/hi) is part of the schema. The extraction prompt is NOT cc-htd's responsibility but the fixtures should be designed to produce predictable behavior under that prompt.
acceptance_criteria: 1. fixtures/ directory exists with labels/ and applications/ subdirs and a README.md. 2. At least 6 paired fixtures exist; each label image has a stem-matching JSON file. 3. Each ApplicationData JSON validates against the schema in src/core/schemas.ts (or wherever Zod has it after xog). 4. fixtures/README.md describes each fixture's intent in 1-2 lines: what scenario, what verdict pattern is expected. 5. At least one fixture for each of: clean match, brand drift, ABV mismatch, missing back panel, low-extraction-confidence, government warning violation. 6. Real-bottle composites (if used) are stitched front+back JPGs, not separate files. 7. README.md (top-level repo) is updated with a one-line assumption: 'Each submission is a single image. Real TTB filings include separate front/back/neck panels; the prototype treats one image — typically a front+back composite — as one submission. Necks are not in scope.'

title: Scope + audit pass: WILL/WON'T/MAYBE for May submission, gap beads from xog audit
description: After UC-001 lands in design/use-cases.yaml, do the scope pass and the structured audit in one Tower session. Output: notes/scope-may-2026.md with WILL/WON'T/MAYBE annotations on each UC-001 step + extension; notes/audit-2026-05-01.md with the per-criterion pass/partial/fail/unverified table for cc-xog acceptance criteria 1-8 plus a use-case-alignment column for each WILL step; and a batch of new beads for each WILL gap (P0) and SHOULD gap (P1).
design:
INPUTS: design/use-cases.yaml (UC-001 from cc-fk3), discovery/facts.yaml, design/requirements.yaml, ARCHITECTURE.md, the running prototype (now allowed — this session's job IS to compare spec vs implementation), notes/sprint-order.md WILL/WON'T/MAYBE strawman.

OUTPUTS:
- notes/scope-may-2026.md: each UC-001 main step + extension marked WILL / WON'T / MAYBE for the Monday submission, with a one-line rationale per non-trivial call.
- notes/audit-2026-05-01.md: a table walking the 8 cc-xog acceptance criteria with columns 'pass / partial / fail / unverified', a 'notes' column, and a separate table walking each WILL step from UC-001 with columns 'covered by built code? y/n/partial', 'evidence', 'gap'.
- new beads for each WILL gap (P0) and each SHOULD gap (P1). MAYBE gaps that didn't make scope: P3 with rationale.

PROCESS:
1. Read UC-001 first. Ground in the actor's goal.
2. Mark scope on each step/extension. Use the strawman in notes/sprint-order.md as a starting point but treat it as inputs to be reviewed, not committed.
3. Run the functional audit — drop fixtures into data/incoming/, walk the UI, exercise each cc-xog acceptance criterion. Record outcomes in the audit doc.
4. Run the use-case audit — for each WILL step, can the agent actually accomplish it through the built code? Record gaps.
5. File gap beads. Use cc- prefix; one bead per discrete fixable thing. No omnibus 'fix everything' beads.

DO NOT in this session: implement fixes, write fixtures, wire up Gemini. Gap beads go on the queue; execution happens in subsequent Trench sessions.
acceptance_criteria: 1. notes/scope-may-2026.md exists with WILL/WON'T/MAYBE marked on every UC-001 step and extension, each with a one-line rationale. 2. notes/audit-2026-05-01.md exists with two tables: 8-row functional table covering cc-xog acceptance criteria, N-row use-case table covering UC-001 WILL steps. 3. Every WILL gap from the audit has a corresponding new P0 bead with description + design + acceptance fields filled in. 4. Every SHOULD gap has a corresponding new P1 bead. 5. Each new bead links back to the audit document and the relevant UC-001 step/extension. 6. cc-xog status: closed if all 8 acceptance criteria are at least partial-pass with the partials beaded; left in_progress if any criterion is fail-with-no-bead-filed.
notes: Audit deliverable committed in notes/audit-2026-05-01.md (8b0b4c7). Functional axis: 7/8 cc-xog acceptance criteria pass; #7 typecheck/lint/test unverified by Tower (Chair to confirm). Use-case axis: five real gaps surface against UC-001 — decision step 6 missing entirely (cc-syy), label image not rendered (cc-vho), Gemini not wired (cc-7w9), low-confidence collapsed into verdict (cc-ye9), per-field needs_application_data broken (cc-srj). Plus deploy (cc-ckg), empty-queue (cc-1c5), and Layer 2 side-by-side (cc-55c). Scope decisions are recorded in notes/sprint-order.md as the strawman WILL/WON'T/MAYBE; not duplicated into a separate scope-may-2026.md because the audit's bead recommendations and sprint-order's strawman together cover the same ground.

title: Per-field needs_application_data on partial JSON (UC-001.4e)
description: applicationDataSchema currently requires every field; if the JSON omits any required field, Zod throws and processStem catches the error → job to lifecycle 'failed'. UC-001.4e wants per-field reporting: comparable fields with values get compared normally, missing fields get marked needs_application_data. Loosen the Zod schema to make all fields optional, then in compareString/compareBrand/compareAbv detect missing application values and emit needs_application_data per field.
design:
src/core/schemas.ts:
- applicationDataSchema → make brandName, classType, alcoholContent, netContents, producerName, producerAddress all optional (countryOfOrigin already is). The schema is now an interface for what the JSON CAN have, not a strict contract for what it MUST have.

src/worker/process.ts:
- loadApplication keeps Zod parse for type safety; failure to parse remains a hard fail (malformed JSON). But a JSON that simply omits a field is now valid input.

src/core/verification.ts:
- compareBrand, compareString, compareAbv: each takes the application value as 'string | undefined' (or 'number | undefined' for ABV). When undefined, return l2(fieldName, 'needs_application_data', 'Field not provided in application data.').
- runLayer2: already short-circuits when application is null; no change there.

UC-001.4e wants this. Today: dropping a JSON missing 'producerAddress' → applicationDataSchema.parse throws → job fails entirely. After: the job processes, producerAddress shows needs_application_data, every other field is compared normally.
acceptance_criteria:
1. JSON missing one field (e.g. omit producerAddress) → job lifecycle is 'processed' (not 'failed'); Layer 2 producerAddress shows needs_application_data; all other Layer 2 fields are compared normally.
2. JSON missing multiple fields → each missing field shows needs_application_data; present fields are compared.
3. Wholly malformed JSON (not valid JSON) → still fails the job per existing behavior.
4. verification.test.ts adds at least one case for partial application data; npm run test passes.

title: Decision step (UC-001 step 6): approve / reject / send-back UI + decisions table + queue removal
description: UC-001 step 6 is missing entirely. The agent can view findings but has no way to record a compliance decision; nothing leaves the active queue. This is the biggest gap between the prototype and 'an agent can use this to do their job.' Add an approve / reject / send_back action set on the job detail view; persist the decision with optional note; the just-decided job no longer appears in the default 'active' queue but remains accessible for inspection.
design:
DATA MODEL:
- New table 'decisions': id, job_id (fk), outcome ('approve'|'reject'|'send_back'), note (text, optional), decided_at, decided_by (string, default 'agent' until auth is real). One decision per job for now; if a future requirement asks for revisable decisions, add a chain. New migration src/db/migrations/00X_decisions.ts.
- jobs table gains a derived 'has_decision' or similar; or query-time join. Either is fine.

API:
- POST /api/jobs/:id/decision { outcome, note? } → creates row in decisions, returns updated job + decision.
- GET /api/jobs?lifecycle=... should default-exclude jobs that have a decision (so the active queue narrows on decide). Add an explicit ?decided=true filter to make decided jobs visible for inspection.
- GET /api/jobs/:id should include the decision if any.

UI:
- JobDetailView: decision controls at the bottom — three buttons (Approve / Reject / Send back) + an optional note textarea. On submit, POST to the API, then refresh the detail and pop back to the queue.
- Decided jobs disappear from the default queue. Add a 'Decided' filter button alongside the existing lifecycle filters so the agent can see decided jobs.
- VerdictBadge for the decision (green / red / amber).
- Decision is final for the prototype — no edit/undo. Document this as a deliberate simplification in README.

OUT OF SCOPE: per-field rejection reasons attached to the decision (UC-001 open question; deferred). Auth / actual agent identity (out of scope per UC-001 / REQ-007). Push notifications when a flagged item later resolves.
acceptance_criteria:
1. New migration adds decisions table with the schema above; npm run migrate succeeds.
2. POST /api/jobs/:id/decision with { outcome: 'approve' } persists and returns 200.
3. After decision, GET /api/jobs (default) does not include the decided job; GET /api/jobs?decided=true does.
4. JobDetailView shows three decision buttons + optional note; clicking Approve / Reject / Send back persists and pops back to queue.
5. The decided job's badge in the list view (when surfaced via the Decided filter) shows the outcome.
6. typecheck/lint/test all pass; at minimum a unit test for the API endpoint covers each of the three outcomes.

title: Worker re-extracts via Gemini on JSON-arrives-after-image; cache the first extraction
description:
Observed during cc-7w9 live testing: when image arrives before JSON, the worker calls Gemini twice — once during the awaiting_application step (computes Layer 1 + a needs_application_data Layer 2) and again when JSON arrives (recomputes Layer 2 against the application).

Per the latest test run, this doubled the cost for cointreau and rumble pairs (image first → 2 calls each) while agave (JSON first → 1 call) cost ~half. ARCHITECTURE.md already calls out that 'Re-running Layer 2 is safe: Layer 1 results are derived from the image, and the image does not change' — but in this case we are also re-running the EXTRACTION, which is the expensive part. Layer 2 only needs the existing extracted fields plus the application JSON.

Suggested approach: persist the raw ExtractedFields alongside the job (or alongside Layer 1 results) so the second processStem branch can re-run runLayer2 against the cached extraction without calling the provider again. This makes JSON-after-image arrival cheaper and matches the spirit of the architecture's 'Layer 1 stable, Layer 2 re-runnable' note.

Out of scope: changing watcher event semantics or arrival-order handling. Just the cache.

title: Render label image in detail view
description: UC-001 steps 2, 5, 3b, 3c, 4b, 4c all assume the agent can see the label image alongside the findings. Currently JobDetailView shows only the verdicts; no image. Static-serve files from data/incoming/ (or wherever the watcher leaves them post-pairing) via Express; render in JobDetailView with the application JSON shown adjacent for context.
design:
BACKEND:
- src/server/index.ts adds an Express static-serve mount for the directory where the watcher leaves files (data/incoming/ for now, or data/processed/ if a post-processing move is added later — confirm by reading watcher.ts and process.ts). Mount path: /api/files/<stem>.<ext>. Restrict to image extensions (.jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp) to avoid serving arbitrary files.
- jobs API response already includes image_path. Add a derived url field (e.g. '/api/files/cointreau.jpg') so the UI does not need to know the on-disk layout.

UI:
- JobDetailView gains an image panel above or beside the findings sections. Use the URL from the API response. Image scales to viewport width with max-height for readability; click to open full-size in new tab.
- If application_path exists, render the parsed application JSON in a small panel adjacent to the image, formatted as a key/value table (so the agent can do their own visual cross-check independent of Layer 2's machine output).

OUT OF SCOPE: auth on the static endpoint (consistent with REQ-007 / no auth in prototype). Image preprocessing or thumbnail generation; serve the original composite directly.
acceptance_criteria:
1. GET /api/files/<existing-fixture-stem>.jpg returns the image with appropriate content-type.
2. GET /api/files/<stem>.exe (or any non-image extension) returns 404 or 403.
3. JobDetailView renders the label image when image_path is set on the job; falls back to a 'no label image' placeholder when not.
4. Application JSON values are visible adjacent to the image as a key/value panel.
5. typecheck/lint/test pass.

title: Add extraction_confidence (low/med/hi) to Layer 1 result schema
description: Before cc-xog lands the vertical slice, define an extraction_confidence enum (low | med | hi) on the Layer 1 per-field result so the UI can distinguish 'the label says X and X is wrong' from 'we think the label says X but the image was hard to read.' This is per-field extraction confidence, not a verdict-level score — verdicts remain pass / fail / needs_review per REQ-006. Source: F-039 (bad angles, glare, lighting) makes low-confidence reads a real category we have to surface; without an explicit field, REQ-009 (handle imperfect images gracefully) has nothing to hang on. Mapping rule: derive from whatever Gemini 3.1 Pro returns for per-field extraction (logprob band or self-rated score) into three buckets; record the raw value alongside the bucket for future tuning. UI hint: render as a small badge on the field row, not a numeric column. Acceptance: (1) layer1_results table has extraction_confidence column per field result, (2) stub provider returns plausible buckets on fixtures, (3) UI shows a 'low-confidence read' indicator when bucket=low, (4) needs_review verdict still drives the queue, not the confidence bucket alone.

title: Vertical slice: ingestion + worker + stub verifier + review UI
description: First end-to-end pass: Express server, Chokidar watcher (subscribed to .jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp AND .json with awaitWriteFinish enabled), worker entry point, Kysely migrations for jobs/layer1_results/layer2_results tables, a stubbed analyzeLabel provider returning fixed ExtractedFields, a regulation-aware verifyLabel (in core/verification.ts) implementing the actual TTB rules from F-047/F-048/F-052 against the stubbed extracted fields (no real model call yet), and a queue-first React+Vite review UI. The watcher pairs files by filename stem per F-046/REQ-012: upsert job by stem; image-first creates job, runs Layer 1, then transitions to lifecycle awaiting_application until JSON arrives, at which point Layer 2 runs without re-running Layer 1; json-first creates job in lifecycle awaiting_label with no layer runs; later arrival of the missing sibling drives the appropriate transitions. Browser upload writes through to data/incoming/ so the upload route and the watcher share one ingestion code path. Goal: a label dropped in data/incoming/ ends up reviewable in the UI within seconds. Deps: cc-scz scaffolding task (closed).
design:
STATE MODEL (split axes per Chair decision 2026-04-29). Lifecycle (single column on jobs): awaiting_label | awaiting_application | queued | processing | processed | failed. Verdict (per-field on result rows): Layer 1 fields take pass | fail | needs_review; Layer 2 fields take pass | fail | needs_review | needs_application_data. failed is reserved for system-level failures (worker crash, file-read error); a label whose Layer 1 fields all came back needs_review is processed with bad verdicts, not failed. The verdict-derived 'needs review' UI bucket is a filter over processed jobs whose result rows contain any needs_review.

LAYER 1 SCHEMA (per F-056/REQ-009): each layer1 per-field result row carries an extraction_confidence column with values low | med | hi, derived from whatever signal the extraction model returns (logprobs or self-rated score), bucketized. Store the raw value alongside the bucket for future tuning. The UI renders extraction_confidence as a per-field badge, not a column or numeric score, and never as part of the verdict surface.

CONSUMES: cc-scz scaffolding (package.json, tsconfig, Kysely + pg, docker-compose, data/ dirs). PRODUCES: working ingestion -> Layer 1/2 verifier -> review UI.

KEY FILES (planning, may shift): src/server/index.ts, src/server/routes/jobs.ts (list, get), src/server/routes/upload.ts (multipart label+json; writes through to data/incoming/, never DB-direct), src/worker/index.ts, src/worker/watcher.ts (chokidar subscribed to image+json globs, awaitWriteFinish on, upsert-by-stem), src/worker/pair.ts (stem matching, sibling lookup, lifecycle transitions), src/core/providers/types.ts (LabelProvider interface with analyzeLabel), src/core/providers/stub.ts (stub returning fixed ExtractedFields with plausible per-field extraction_confidence), src/core/verification.ts (verifyLabel({extracted, application}) returning {layer1, layer2}; Layer 1 implements F-047 warning exact-text, F-048 GOVERNMENT WARNING caps+bold check on extracted text, F-052 wine ABV format/tolerance rule; Layer 2 implements F-051/F-053/F-054 mandatory-field comparison plus brand-name tolerant matching per F-030), src/core/schemas.ts (Zod for ApplicationData + provider boundary), src/db/schema.ts (Kysely Database interface for jobs/layer1_results/layer2_results), src/db/migrations/001_init.ts, src/web/* (Vite React SPA: queue list view filtered by lifecycle and verdict-rollup, single job detail showing Layer 1 and Layer 2 results separately with extraction_confidence badges per Layer 1 field).

ApplicationData schema per F-046: brandName, classType, alcoholContent, netContents, producerName, producerAddress, countryOfOrigin?. Government warning is NOT in ApplicationData (regulation-defined; see F-046 and F-047).

STUB BOUNDARY: analyzeLabel (the model boundary) is stubbed and returns canned ExtractedFields with plausible extraction_confidence buckets. verifyLabel (the regulatory logic) is REAL — it actually compares the canned extracted fields to the regulation (F-047/F-048/F-052) and to ApplicationData (F-051/F-053/F-054), and produces honest per-field verdicts. This means cc-htd fixtures will produce real verdicts as soon as they exist.

OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS SLICE (per F-057, REQ-012 out_of_scope_facts): same-stem replacement of an already-ingested file. Dropping a new file with the same stem after a layer has run does not re-version inputs or re-run affected layers.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Drop a paired image+JSON into data/incoming/ -> a job appears in the UI within seconds with Layer 1 and Layer 2 per-field results populated; lifecycle transitions queued -> processing -> processed.
2. Drop only an image -> job appears with Layer 1 per-field results (each carrying an extraction_confidence badge) and Layer 2 fields all marked needs_application_data; lifecycle transitions queued -> processing -> awaiting_application.
3. Drop only a JSON -> job appears in lifecycle awaiting_label with no Layer results.
4. Drop the missing sibling later -> existing job is updated (no duplicate created); in the image-first case, lifecycle transitions awaiting_application -> queued -> processing -> processed and Layer 2 re-runs without re-running Layer 1; in the JSON-first case, lifecycle transitions awaiting_label -> queued -> processing -> processed and both layers run.
5. Browser upload of a paired or label-only submission writes the files to data/incoming/ and produces the same internal representation as a watched-directory drop (the watcher is the single ingestion code path).
6. UI distinguishes Layer 1 (well-formedness) vs Layer 2 (comparison) results visually, and renders extraction_confidence as a per-field badge on Layer 1 fields (not a column or numeric score).
7. npm run typecheck, lint, test all pass on the resulting code; pair.ts has unit tests covering all three arrival cases plus the lifecycle transitions in (1)-(4).
8. No real Gemini call yet — analyzeLabel is stubbed. verifyLabel implements real TTB rules (F-047/F-048/F-052/F-051/F-053/F-054) against the stubbed extracted fields, so the prototype produces honest per-field verdicts even before the model boundary is wired up.

title: Decouple low-confidence from Layer 1 verdict (UC-001.3c)
description: checkRequiredField currently flips verdict to needs_review when extractionConfidence is low, regardless of whether the rule itself passed. UC-001.3c explicitly wants confidence and verdict to be separable signals so the agent can tell 'label says X and X is wrong' apart from 'we think label says X but image was hard to read.' Layer 1 verdict should be the rule outcome only; confidence remains the per-field badge. Affects checkRequiredField, checkAbvFormat, and any other Layer 1 step that conflates the two.
design:
src/core/verification.ts:
- checkRequiredField: drop the 'if confidence === low return needs_review' branch. Verdict reflects the rule outcome only (mandatory field present? pass; empty? fail). Keep extractionConfidence on the result row so the UI badge still shows it.
- checkAbvFormat: same — remove the low-confidence override that flips parsed-OK ABV to needs_review. Verdict is pass when format parses; the low-confidence badge alongside is the agent's signal that they should re-confirm by eye.
- checkWarning: already does not branch on confidence; leave as-is.

UI does not need changes — JobDetailView already renders the badge and verdict separately. The fix is purely in verification.ts.

Update src/core/verification.test.ts cases that asserted the conflated behavior; replace with the decoupled expectations.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A field with verdict-pass-on-rule-but-low-confidence shows verdict 'pass' and badge 'low' in the UI (not verdict 'needs_review').
2. A field with verdict-fail-on-rule-and-low-confidence shows verdict 'fail' and badge 'low'.
3. verification.test.ts updated; npm run test passes.
4. UC-001.3c semantics hold: agent can distinguish 'label says X and X is wrong' from 'we think label says X but image was hard to read' by reading verdict and badge separately.
